reviews.review: Great take on a fps roguelite. There aren't a ton of levels but there are enough characters/modifiers/difficulties to keep it interesting for a long time. Also worth noting, it's still actively being supported!

Highly recommended, while generally not a roguelike fan I consider this one very good. The obvious and easy comparison is to Borderlands, and I think they've done a very good job adapting some of the ideas from the game to a roguelike formula.

Each character has 2 skills, each with a designated skill tree. Most of them are interesting, especially the more recent ones, and depending on the character they can be independently useful or have amazing synergy with each other.

Skill tree passives are called "Ascensions" and are given at set intervals in progression and will contain 3 randomly selected ones, of which you get to pick 1. Most of them are good enough that you will infrequently feel like you've been completely robbed.

The generic passives are called "Occult Scrolls" and are similarly found at set intervals in progression, sometimes in sets of 3 and sometimes only 1, can be bought from the peddler, and also drop from elite and boss enemies. Again, much like ascensions, they are balanced well enough that you almost never feel like you've just gotten shafted. Unlike ascensions you get more of these per run, and the pool is just comfortable enough that you can count on finding some of the common and rare ones you're looking for every time.

The weapon design is varied and has a few standout interesting ones. The balance for weapons is much worse than the other two character building components, but not so much so that you'll ever be stuck with a "bad" base weapon. You'll find one of the ones you like with good rolls every run. Rolls are (almost) all good and are usually your standard number-go-up fare, with some weapons having their own unique ones that might buff its unique function.

Enemy design is good, nothing has hitscan attacks so you never feel like damage is COMPLETELY unavoidable. Bosses die way too quickly. Don't have a lot to say here.

Current issues: The latter half of the game is almost always too easy, difficulty drops off very sharply after acts 1 and 2. The new "Bizarre Dream" feature is great, makes runs more interesting and in some ways more consistent, but some of them are way too strong compared to their drawbacks and make the game much easier. Spiritual Link has no drawbacks and is insanely strong, but does make the game more interesting and should probably just be a base feature. The drawback of Lone Wolf is completely offset by how strong some of the Spiritual Blessings are, but the feature itself is fine. Independent Fortunes gives too many scrolls and most of the drawbacks are ignorable. The others are fine how they are, and are all pretty cool. The status effect "Miasma" is inflicted by using the two status effects best suited for shields/armor, but if the enemy has all of their health converted to either of those then it becomes completely useless and only does 1 damage. The "point blank" challenge event should be tuned down or removed.

Things I would like to see: extra ascension and weapon rerolls, you can only reroll either under very specific circumstances, even 1 free one per run would be a welcome addition.
this is THE most roguelike of all time
